notes: Vela v1.0 Pre-release (opt-in). This build is about memory. HTTPS transfers were failing with a bare errno, because mbedTLS reports an out-of-memory as OSError(ENOMEM) rather than MemoryError and the guidance was only ever wired to MemoryError; and the pre-handshake contiguous-block check guarded 10 KB when a handshake needs about 16.7 KB, so it passed and the handshake died anyway. Both fixed. wget no longer rebuilds the whole response body on every chunk (about 40 KB of churn to fetch 6 KB), which was fragmenting the heap in exactly the place a handshake needs an unbroken run. meminfo now reports the largest allocatable block and a fragmentation percentage, because free memory alone is what made "90 KB free" and "cannot do HTTPS" look contradictory. New 'defrag' command reclaims and reports whether a handshake can start; optional 'defrag on' holds a contiguous block from boot (off by default, applies after a reboot). Pre-release — please report bugs.
features: Fixed: an HTTPS out-of-memory now explains itself. mbedTLS raises OSError(ENOMEM), not MemoryError, so the actionable message was dead code for the exact case it was written for

Fixed: the pre-handshake contiguous-block check guarded 10 KB, but MBEDTLS_SSL_IN_CONTENT_LEN is 16384 and the input buffer is one allocation — the check passed on a heap that could not finish a handshake
Fixed: wget rebuilt the entire response body on every chunk (twelve growing allocations, ~40 KB of churn for a 6 KB file), fragmenting the heap right after a handshake had taken its block
meminfo now reports the LARGEST ALLOCATABLE BLOCK and a fragmentation percentage, not just free memory — the GC never compacts, so free memory alone is misleading
New: defrag — reclaim and report whether there is enough contiguous RAM for HTTPS; defrag on|auto|off holds a block from boot (off by default)
New: safeboot [cmd] can STAGE an update to run on a serviceless maintenance boot (full RAM), then reboot back — reliable UI updates
Fixed: removing a package also removes its startup task + background service
Fixed: pkg install streams the archive to flash (512-byte chunks) — no more MemoryError on large packages; a partly-extracted package registers no command
DEVELOPER BUILD — the v0.9.5 multitasking foundation, now the default experience
Multitasking shell is the DEFAULT — background services keep running while you work (classic sync shell stays as the recovery / crash fallback)
Background services: httpd start --bg / status / stop; service list/add/remove/test
Cooperative app framework (appkit) — a foreground app (e.g. sysmon) yields so it runs alongside background services
Full async line editor — history, Tab completion, cursor + word navigation (shared LineEditor with the classic shell)
